title: Projective sections of an enriched Quillen diagram and its coherent localization
statement:
Here a combinatorial differential graded model category means a locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups (with cochain differentials and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), with cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three, closure under retracts, and functorial factorizations into (cofibration, trivial fibration) and (trivial cofibration, fibration), with the corresponding lifting properties. The two weak factorization systems are generated by sets. Enrichment satisfies the model compatibility axiom: for a cofibration $i$ and a fibration $p$, the induced map of Hom complexes is a fibration in the projective model structure on complexes of abelian groups, trivial if $i$ or $p$ is trivial. Trivial means also a weak equivalence. Stable means that the enhanced localization has a zero object and finite homotopy limits and colimits, and its homotopy pushout squares are exactly its homotopy pullback squares. A differential graded Quillen adjunction is an enriched adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Its enhanced localization retains derived mapping complexes and all composition homotopies; equivalently one may use the associated stable homotopy theory with its chain enrichment when the model category is stable.

Let $I$ be a small category, let $\mathcal M_i$ be stable combinatorial differential graded model categories, and for every arrow $\alpha:i\to j$ let $F_\alpha:\mathcal M_i\rightleftarrows\mathcal M_j:U_\alpha$ be a differential graded Quillen adjunction. Specify coherent enriched isomorphisms $F_\beta F_\alpha\cong F_{\beta\alpha}$ and $F_{1_i}\cong\mathrm{id}$, satisfying associativity and unit identities. A strict section is a family $X_i$ and maps $F_\alpha X_i\to X_j$ satisfying those identities; a map of sections is a compatible componentwise map. The category $\operatorname{Sect}(F)$ has a combinatorial differential graded projective model structure with weak equivalences and fibrations detected at every $i$. Cofibrant sections have cofibrant evaluations. Evaluation at $i$ has a left adjoint $E_i$ given by
$$ (E_i A)_j=\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}F_\alpha A.$$

The enhanced localization of $\operatorname{Sect}(F)$ at componentwise weak equivalences is equivalent, over the evaluations, to the category of homotopy coherent sections of the diagram of enhanced localizations $\mathbf L\mathcal M_i$ and derived functors $\mathbf L F_\alpha$. A homotopy coherent section consists of objects $X_i$, arrows $\mathbf L F_\alpha X_i\to X_j$, and composition homotopies for every composable string, with higher compatibility homotopies. Its mapping complex is the homotopy coherent end of the component mapping complexes: degree $r$ of its cosimplicial replacement is
$$\prod_{i_0\xrightarrow{\alpha_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{\alpha_r}i_r}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M_{i_r}}(\mathbf L F_{\alpha_r\cdots\alpha_1}X_{i_0},Y_{i_r}).$$
The end is the derived totalization, retaining all matching homotopies, rather than an underived equalizer. The comparison preserves these mapping complexes and composition. Equivalences between coherent sections are detected componentwise.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, enriched finite coefficient adjunction before the inverse limit: generic rectification foundation formulated by the agent. No Stacks tag in the supplied sources states this enriched Quillen-diagram theorem. WANTED: an enriched/differential graded version of the lax-limit rectification theorem (compare Harpaz, Lax limits of model categories, main rectification theorem).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=\prod_i\mathcal M_i$. Define an endofunctor $T_0$ by $(T_0A)_j=\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}F_\alpha A_i$. The summand of $T_0^2A$ indexed by $i\xrightarrow\alpha j\xrightarrow\beta k$ maps by $F_\beta F_\alpha\cong F_{\beta\alpha}$ to the $(\beta\alpha)$-summand of $T_0A$. Identity-arrow summands give its unit. The supplied associativity and unit identities give the monad identities on each coproduct summand. An algebra action is precisely a family $F_\alpha A_i\to A_j$; its unit and multiplication equations are precisely the section equations. Algebra morphisms are precisely compatible maps of sections. Every $F_\alpha$ preserves small colimits since it is a left adjoint, so $T_0$ does too, in particular sufficiently filtered colimits. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-monad-presentability] to obtain local presentability, completeness and cocompleteness of $\operatorname{Sect}(F)$. Colimits are componentwise: for a diagram of sections take each fiber colimit, use $F_\alpha\operatorname{colim}\cong\operatorname{colim}F_\alpha$ to define its transitions, and check the section identities after each cocone leg. A map out of this family is a section map exactly when its composites with all legs are, proving the colimit universal property.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: free-section monad and presentability

proof.text: For $i$ and $A\in\mathcal M_i$, give $(E_iA)_j=\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}F_\alpha A$ the transition along $\beta:j\to k$ which carries the $\alpha$-summand by the supplied isomorphism to the $\beta\alpha$-summand. The coherence identities make it a section. An enriched map $E_iA\to X$ is determined by its restriction to the identity summand at $i$; from $a:A\to X_i$, its $\alpha$-component is $F_\alpha A\xrightarrow{F_\alpha a}F_\alpha X_i\to X_j$. These assignments are inverse in every degree of the Hom complexes and commute with differentials and composition. Thus $E_i\dashv\mathrm{ev}_i$ is an enriched adjunction. Write $L(A)=\coprod_iE_iA_i$; then $L\dashv U$, where $U$ is the family of evaluations and $UL=T_0$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: explicit free sections and evaluation adjunction

proof.text: Choose generating cofibrations $C_i$ and generating trivial cofibrations $J_i$ in every fiber. They give sets $C=\{E_i c:c\in C_i\}$ and $J=\{E_i t:t\in J_i\}$. The adjunction in step 2 shows $C^\square$ is exactly the componentwise trivial fibrations and $J^\square$ exactly the componentwise fibrations. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-small-object-factorization] separately to $C$ and $J$ in the locally presentable section category. This supplies both functorial factorizations, with left classes ${}^\square(C^\square)$ and ${}^\square(J^\square)$. To control evaluations of these classes, apply [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization]: factor any map of either left class as a cellular map for that set followed by a map of its right class. Its lifting property exhibits it as a retract of the cellular factor. Evaluation preserves the coproducts, pushouts and ordinal colimits in this factorization by step 1, while $\mathrm{ev}_j(E_i c)=\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}F_\alpha c$ is a cofibration, trivial if $c$ is trivial. Indeed coproducts, pushouts, transfinite composites and retracts of a fixed left lifting class remain in that class: solve the coproduct/pushout lifting problems componentwise, extend a lift at successors, take its colimit at limits, and compose with the retraction. It follows that the two left classes evaluate to cofibrations and trivial cofibrations respectively.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: two generated factorizations and evaluation of cofibrations

proof.text: Let $W$ denote componentwise weak equivalences and let $\mathrm{Cof}={}^\square(C^\square)$. Step 3 gives ${}^\square(J^\square)\subseteq\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$: a lift against all fibrations is a lift against trivial fibrations, and every evaluated map of this class is trivial. Conversely factor $f\in\mathrm{Cof}\cap W$ using $J$ as $f=pj$. The first map $j$ belongs to $W$, so two-out-of-three makes the componentwise fibration $p$ a componentwise trivial fibration. Lifting $f$ against $p$ expresses $f$ as a retract of $j$, so $f\in{}^\square(J^\square)$. Thus the two functorial weak factorization systems are exactly $(\mathrm{Cof},\mathrm{Fib}\cap W)$ and $(\mathrm{Cof}\cap W,\mathrm{Fib})$. The componentwise two-out-of-three and retract axioms prove the model axioms. Step 1 gives all limits and colimits, and step 3 gives generation by sets, so the model is combinatorial. A cofibrant section has cofibrant evaluations by applying step 3 to its initial map.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: model axioms by the explicit retract argument

proof.text: The section Hom complex is the subcomplex of $\prod_i\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X_i,Y_i)$ cut out by compatibility with every arrow. Tensors and cotensors by a complex $K$ are componentwise. For tensors use $F_\alpha(K\otimes X_i)\cong K\otimes F_\alpha X_i$; this isomorphism follows from the enriched left adjunction. For cotensors the map $F_\alpha(X_i^K)\to(F_\alpha X_i)^K$ is adjoint to $K\otimes F_\alpha(X_i^K)\cong F_\alpha(K\otimes X_i^K)\to F_\alpha X_i$. This defines the section structure and the tensor--Hom--cotensor adjunctions. For a cofibration $a$ of complexes and a free generating cofibration $E_i c$, their pushout product is $a\mathbin\square E_i c\cong E_i(a\mathbin\square c)$. The fiber enriched model axiom, transposed through tensor--Hom, says this is a section cofibration, trivial if $a$ or $c$ is trivial. The cellular/retract characterization of step 3 extends this to every section cofibration: tensor and pushout product preserve the displayed coproducts, pushouts and transfinite colimits in the section variable, and preserve retracts. Use $J$-cells for a trivial section cofibration. Transposing the resulting pushout-product lifting assertions back proves the required fibration and trivial-fibration assertions for section Hom complexes. Thus the projective model is differential graded.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: enriched model compatibility checked on free cells

proof.text: There is also an enriched right adjoint $R_i$ to $\mathrm{ev}_i$, given by $(R_iA)_j=\prod_{\gamma:j\to i}U_\gamma A$. For $\beta:j\to k$, its structure in right-adjoint form is the map $(R_iA)_j\to U_\beta(R_iA)_k$ whose $\gamma:k\to i$ projection is the $\gamma\beta$ projection, using $U_{\gamma\beta}\cong U_\beta U_\gamma$ and preservation of products by $U_\beta$. For $\beta:j\to k$, $\delta:k\to l$ and $\gamma:l\to i$, both successive transition maps, followed by the $\gamma$ projection, are the $\gamma\delta\beta$ projection of $(R_iA)_j$, identified with $U_\beta U_\delta U_\gamma A$ by the supplied right-adjoint coherence. The given associativity identity identifies these two projections; the identity-arrow projection gives the unit identity. A map $X\to R_iA$ is determined by $X_i\to A$ at the identity projection; its other projections are the adjoints of the composites $F_\gamma X_j\to X_i\to A$. This proves the adjunction on Hom complexes. Step 3 makes $\mathrm{ev}_i$ left Quillen, and step 4 makes it right Quillen. The family $U$ is likewise both: its left adjoint is $L$, its right adjoint is $A\mapsto\prod_iR_iA_i$, and its preservation assertions are componentwise. It already preserves all weak equivalences.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: right evaluation adjoints and both Quillen directions

proof.text: Let $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Sect}(F)[W^{-1}]$ and $\mathcal C=\prod_i(\mathcal M_i[W_i^{-1}])$. Give $\mathcal P$ the componentwise model classes and factorizations. Lifting problems and retracts are componentwise, so these satisfy the model axioms. If $H_i$ inserts an object in coordinate $i$ and initial objects elsewhere, the sets $\{H_i c:c\in C_i\}$ and $\{H_i t:t\in J_i\}$ generate its two right lifting classes, by $H_i\dashv\mathrm{ev}_i$; factorizations exist componentwise. Its local presentability was proved in step 1. Its Hom complexes are products, and tensors and cotensors are componentwise. The enriched model axiom follows because products of degreewise surjections are surjections and products of acyclic complexes of abelian groups are acyclic: choose a primitive in each coordinate. Thus this is a combinatorial dg model category. The product model category on $\mathcal P$ presents $\mathcal C$: its bifibrant objects are tuples of bifibrant objects and its mapping complex is the product of the fiber mapping complexes. Apply [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison] to $\mathcal P$ and to the section model of step 5. It computes each mapping object by cofibrant source and fibrant target. Products of complexes here also compute derived products: a degreewise surjection remains surjective under products, products preserve acyclicity by taking primitives coordinatewise, and all complexes are fibrant. Every tuple in $\mathcal C$ has a tuple of bifibrant representatives, so these mapping calculations give the asserted product presentation. The enriched adjunction $L\dashv U$ therefore induces a derived enriched adjunction $\mathbb L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:\mathbb U$. More explicitly the strict isomorphism $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(LP,Y)=\prod_i\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P_i,Y_i)$ computes its derived adjunction for cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $Y$, since $LP$ is cofibrant and $UY$ fibrant. Localizing these relative bifunctors and their strict adjunction transformations by [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] retains units, counits and every coherence diagram. The same argument for the second adjunction in step 6 makes $\mathbb U$ a left adjoint as well. Its two derived versions agree with direct localization because $U$ preserves all weak equivalences. On underlying infinity categories this is also [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction].

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: derived enriched free/evaluation adjunctions and product presentation

proof.text: By [lem-coef-dg-model-homotopy-colimits], $\mathcal D$ and every fiber localization have small colimits, in particular geometric realizations, with the enriched mapping-object universal property. The product $\mathcal C$ has these colimits componentwise: its mapping objects are products, and the limit defining a colimit universal property commutes with a product by its own universal property. Since $\mathbb U$ is a left adjoint as well as a right adjoint by step 7, it preserves colimits. Explicitly, if $\mathbb V$ is its right adjoint, maps from $\mathbb U\operatorname{colim}A$ to $B$ identify by adjunction with maps from $\operatorname{colim}A$ to $\mathbb VB$, hence with the limit of maps from each $\mathbb UA_j$ to $B$. This characterizes the colimit comparison and all its coherences. Also $\mathbb U$ is conservative. Represent a morphism of $\mathcal D$ using a closed degree-zero map between bifibrant sections, possible by [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison]. If its evaluations are equivalences, saturation in [lem-coef-dg-model-homotopy-colimits] makes each component a weak equivalence in its model category; the representative is then in $W$ by definition, hence the original morphism is an equivalence. These arguments verify, rather than assume, the two monadicity hypotheses. Here colimits mean initial objects in the coherent comma cocone categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the diagram indexed by its nerve when the index is ordinary. The conservativity conclusion uses equivalence edges, with coherent inverse witnesses, in those underlying quasicategories; it does not replace coherent cocones by cocones in the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: geometric realizations and conservativity

proof.text:
Compute the monad $\mathbb T=\mathbb U\mathbb L$ on $\mathcal C$. For a tuple of cofibrant representatives $P_i$, step 2 gives $(ULP)_j=\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}F_\alpha P_i$. Its summands are cofibrant. Coproduct of cofibrant replacements computes the derived coproduct: coproduct is left Quillen from the discrete product model, since its right adjoint diagonal preserves (trivial) fibrations. Thus
$$(\mathbb T A)_j\simeq\coprod_{\alpha:i\to j}\mathbf L F_\alpha A_i.$$
Its unit includes the identity summands, and its multiplication sends the $(\alpha,\beta)$ summand by the derived given comparison to the $\beta\alpha$ summand. This description includes all composition coherence: the iterated source on cofibrant $P_i$ is a coproduct of iterated left-Quillen images, again cofibrant; hence all the original associativity and unit diagrams are diagrams on the same homotopical domain. [lem-coef-dg-derived-quillen-calculus] supplies the coherent derived composition comparisons, and [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] localizes those diagrams together. In particular this identifies the monad, including its multiplication, rather than only its endofunctor.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: derived monad with the specified composition coherences

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monadic-bar] to the adjunction of step 7 using step 8: its comparison identifies the underlying infinity category of $\mathcal D$ with $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathbb T}(\mathcal C)$ over evaluations. Expanding the algebra data gives exactly the coherent sections in the statement. Indeed an action $\mathbb T A\to A$ is a map $\mathbf L F_\alpha A_i\to A_j$ for each arrow. A summand of $\mathbb T^r A$ is indexed by a length-$r$ composable string. The associativity homotopy on $\mathbb T^2 A$ is the comparison between composing the two section arrows and using their composite arrow; on $\mathbb T^r A$, the higher action compatibilities are the homotopies between all bracketings and contractions of that string. Inserting the monad unit inserts an identity arrow, so the unital compatibility is precisely the degeneracy compatibility. Conversely the coherent section data on all strings define these maps and compatibilities on each summand and hence on their coproducts. This correspondence also applies to parameter simplices of transformations, with faces and degeneracies restricting those same data, so it identifies the coherent categories and their comparison functors. The comparison of a strict section is the localization of its specified structure maps, since its algebra action is the derived counit $\mathbb U\epsilon$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: monadic comparison and explicit identification of coherent actions

proof.text: The comparison is enriched as well. By [lem-coef-dg-model-homotopy-colimits] the localizations have derived tensors by $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ and tensor--mapping-object adjunctions. The derived monad of step 9 commutes with these tensors: each $F_\alpha$ commutes with the original chain tensors by its enriched left adjunction, and coproducts do so. Apply the multivariable derived tensor and transformation clauses of [lem-coef-dg-derived-quillen-calculus] in each stable fiber, with cofibrant complexes and cofibrant fiber inputs; this derives the tensor comparison together with its associativity and unit diagrams. Consequently $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathbb T}(\mathcal C)$, equivalently the coherent-section category just described, has tensor $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}A$ defined on components and on every action homotopy by tensoring it and using that monad comparison. To check its tensor adjunction, express a coherent transformation by its compatible maps and homotopies on every composable string. In each string the fiber tensor adjunction moves $K$ from the source to the internal Hom in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. Naturality of that adjunction identifies both endpoint action maps, every interior composition map, and every identity insertion. Taking the coherent limit of these diagrams preserves these adjunctions because $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(K,-)$ is a right adjoint and therefore preserves limits (test the claim against an arbitrary complex and use its tensor adjunction). Thus the component adjunctions identify the full spaces of coherent transformations, including their higher simplices. The comparison commutes with this tensor, since its action is the counit of the enriched adjunction of step 7; [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] retains its naturality diagrams. It therefore induces maps of derived mapping complexes. For every integer $m$, their cohomology in degree $m$ is tested by maps from $\mathbf Z[-m]$, or equivalently by homotopy classes of maps from $\mathbf Z[-m]\otimes^{\mathbf L}X$ to $Y$. The underlying equivalence in step 10 is fully faithful on all these maps, so the comparison induces an isomorphism on every such cohomology group. It is therefore an equivalence on mapping complexes, compatible with composition by its enriched construction. Essential surjectivity is already supplied by step 10.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle enriched adjunction comparison before inverse limit; agent-supplied foundation: chain-enriched comparison detected by shifted free rank-one complexes

proof.text:
For $X\in\mathcal D$, [lem-coef-infinity-monadic-bar] realizes $X$ by the augmented simplicial object $B_rX=\mathbb L\mathbb T^r\mathbb UX$. Its augmentation really realizes $X$, not just an object with the same fiber values: after $\mathbb U$ the extra degeneracy inserts the identity-arrow summand, and the monadicity theorem applies with the verified conservativity and realization preservation. Applying the enriched colimit formula of [lem-coef-dg-model-homotopy-colimits] and the enriched adjunction of step 7 gives
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}^{\mathbf R}_{[r]\in\Delta}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbb T^r\mathbb UX,\mathbb UY).$$
Expand $\mathbb T^r$ using step 9; maps out of each coproduct are the product of the mapping objects by the enriched colimit formula. The degree-$r$ term is exactly
$$\prod_{i_0\xrightarrow{\alpha_1}\cdots\xrightarrow{\alpha_r}i_r}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M_{i_r}}(\mathbf L F_{\alpha_r\cdots\alpha_1}X_{i_0},Y_{i_r}).$$
Interior cofaces compose adjacent arrows. The first endpoint coface uses the structure map of $X$, the last endpoint coface uses that of $Y$, and codegeneracies insert identity arrows. These are the counit faces and unit degeneracies of the bar under the adjunction, so the result is the coherent end, including all matching homotopies. Derived totalization is necessary even for unbounded complexes; no exchange with an underived equalizer is made. The mapping-complex equivalence is natural in both variables. Composition on these totalizations is induced by splitting a string into its initial and final substrings, applying the last-string derived functor to the first mapping component, and composing with the second component. This is the bar diagonal: splitting into three substrings gives the same iterated map in either order, with the associativity homotopies of step 9; insertion of identities gives the unit. Thus it is the composition transported from the enriched comparison of step 11, including all higher compatibilities. Finally equivalences of coherent sections are detected on evaluations, by step 8 and the equivalence over evaluations of steps 10-11. In the conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the bar is a coherent diagram on $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ and its augmentation is a coherent cocone. The bar theorem asserts that this cocone is initial in the specified comma cocone category. The totalization is the dual limiting-cone notion in the enhanced category of complexes. These categorical realizations are distinct from the topological geometric realization used in that definition to define weak homotopy equivalences of simplicial sets.
